name: Kemi Badenoch
role: Leader of the Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition (2024-present); former Secretary of State for Business and Trade (2023-2024) and Minister for Equalities (2021-2022)
summary: A free-market, small-state Conservative and Brexiteer who favours tax and welfare cuts, scrapping net zero legislation and expanding North Sea oil, gas and nuclear. She wants to leave the European Convention on Human Rights, cut legal migration with annual caps, and requires newcomers to assimilate into a common British culture, while rejecting identity politics and ethnic definitions of the nation. She holds that sex is biological, wants single-sex spaces protected, and backs higher defence spending within NATO and the US alliance.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Defends the NHS in general terms and says it depends on a strong economy; no stated position on universal provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Citing a past minimum wage increase as a record is nearby; no stated view on a substantial rise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says she believes in free markets; in 2022 defended the free market as the fairest way of helping people prosper, and in 2026 said the collective wisdom of people beats the central planning of bureaucrats and politicians.

public-ownership.rationale: In 2026 argued the state failed when it ran firms such as British Leyland, Telecom, Airways and Steel, and that bringing back nationalised industry will not restore the good old days.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Conference 2026 line: what people earn belongs to them, not government; pledged cuts and no inheritance tax on the family home; voted against 2024 Budget capital gains tax rises.

unions-good.rationale: As leader attacked Labour's Employment Rights Bill for the biggest expansion of union powers in a generation and called strikes catastrophic for growth; voted for minimum service levels on strikes. Never stated that unions are bad for society as such.

property-fundamental.rationale: Defends home ownership and low taxes; no stated position on how hard property should be to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pushes deregulation (retained-EU-law repeal, regulatory budgets, scrap employment-law burdens), while saying markets need rules against cheating, monopolies and unfair practices.

cut-welfare.rationale: Calls the welfare system broken, promises to cut the welfare bill, and rejects a something-for-nothing culture and sickness benefits for mild anxiety (2026).

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for the Investigatory Powers (Amendment) Bill and covert human intelligence sources bills; announced live facial recognition in crime hotspots in 2026. Terrorism-specific statement not addressed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Announced mandatory police enforcement of drug laws to drive drug use out of public spaces and attacked Greens' approach (2026).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Called the Online Safety Bill legislation for hurt feelings and champions free speech, though says speech must stay within the law.

state-harmful.rationale: Says the state should do the important things and do them well; government should do fewer things but better.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pledges 10,000 more police, tripled stop and search, and defence at 3% of GDP with the biggest troop increase since WWII.

rehabilitation.rationale: Says she wants more criminals in prison, with 50,000 more places and punishment that fits the crime; frames prison around consequences, not rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Said the family, whether born into or built, is the foundation of society; family in different shapes and sizes.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: As minister said the government was proud to pass the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013, but she abstained on extending it to Northern Ireland in 2019.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes herself as pro-choice but not pro-abortion up to full term (2025 post, reported on Wikipedia).

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Told the Commons that history cannot be improved, only learned from, and that black history is not a history of institutional racism; backed action on current disparities.

gender-social-construct.rationale: States that sex is biological and opposes self-ID; no stated position on gender as a social construct.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Says Britain needs a common culture rooted in history, language and institutions and defends British culture and identity.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Pledges binding annual caps on legal migration and says mass migration must end; ran in 2024 on controlling numbers.

free-trade.rationale: Told Cato free trade and markets are about people's freedom to improve their lives; led CPTPP accession as trade secretary.

nation-first.rationale: Said foreign policy should serve the national interest, which always comes first, calling herself a realist not a progressive internationalist.

open-borders.rationale: Says without strong borders there is no country; borders, control and numbers matter.

limit-growth.rationale: Calls growing the economy the central organising principle of the next Conservative government; criticised net zero as unilateral economic disarmament.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Commits to scrap the net zero legislation and calls it irrational and a gift to China, while saying climate change is real. Earlier, as a minister (2024), defended the 2050 target as set by Parliament; her latest position is repeal.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Said in 2026 the UK needs nuclear and will build new small modular reactors; voted for the Nuclear Energy (Financing) Bill third reading in 2022.

experts-over-public.rationale: Says quango and bureaucrat power should answer to elected ministers, and politicians decide while judges interpret.

central-planning.rationale: Said the collective wisdom of people is greater than central planning by bureaucrats and politicians (2026).

tax-inheritance.rationale: Pledged that nobody pays inheritance tax on the family home, a further £1m tax-free for couples, and abolition of inheritance tax when affordable; voted for the Opposition inheritance-tax motion (2026).

basic-income.rationale: Proposes no out-of-work benefits straight from school or university ('if you haven't paid in you shouldn't take out'), a work requirement after six months and a restricted spending card; this is the opposite of an unconditional payment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Told the Cato Institute that protectionism brings poverty rather than nurturing local industry, citing Nigeria's tomato import ban; in 2022 criticised protectionism for special interests.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Praised postwar Conservatives for the 'property owning democracy' and says young people should be able to acquire capital, a house and savings.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: In her maiden speech listed the monarchy with Parliament, Church and family as institutions critics seek to undermine and that she defends.

right-to-secede.rationale: Said only Conservatives will fight for the Union against separatists and criticised opening the door to a second Scottish referendum.

military-superiority.rationale: Wants Britain to reassert itself as a serious power and spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said Britain is multi-racial and that her children are British, rejecting anyone who says they do not belong.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Called the Industrial Revolution the source of a unique period of European prosperity (2023 Telegraph).

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Stated that truth is not relative and is her most important principle (2024).

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called Israel the Jewish homeland and condemned chants implying Jewish homes should be erased; says Israel has a right to defend herself.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Golden rule that half of savings cut the deficit; in 2026 called spending money we don't have reckless; in her 2017 maiden speech urged colleagues to hold their nerve on debt and the deficit.

economic-freedom.rationale: Says she believes in free markets and free trade but that there is more to conservatism than economic liberalism; in 2024 argued there is no division between the cultural and economic spheres in the case for freedom.

force-without-un.rationale: Criticising legal constraints on policy is nearby; no stated position on force without UN approval.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Wants local people prioritised for housing, benefits and school places; one of her five sovereignty tests is putting British citizens first for social housing and public services.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Wants a welfare system where everyone who can work will work, with a get-to-work programme and a back-to-work card after six months without a job.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Pledges to drill for North Sea oil and gas and approve Rosebank, calling it a no-brainer; attacked Labour for shutting down the North Sea.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said newcomers should join the country not change it, with a commission setting the culture they must assimilate into; wants immigrants to uphold British traditions.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Says veterans and serving troops are harassed through the courts, and promised to protect them from malicious prosecution (ECHR exit pitch).

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wants a smaller state but said it should provide social security and does defence, health and welfare; not a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says she believes in equality under the law, with all laws applying equally to all citizens, and rejects sorting people into categories that pit them against each other.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality under the law is a general principle; no stated position on religious civil law.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted for the Strikes (Minimum Service Levels) Bill and regulations for rail, ambulance, fire and border services; criticised Labour's cut in strike notice. Secret ballots and picketing not addressed directly.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says Britain is multi-racial, but that it must not become multicultural, as shared values dissolve.

party-controls-media.rationale: Champions free speech as the lifeblood of democracy and opposes legislating against speech.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: No stated position by her on citizenship waiting periods.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Brexit supporter who said leaving restored democratic control and the right to choose how to be governed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wants alliances strengthened and mocks Greens' wish to leave NATO; US alliance key.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Wrote that one cannot assume all cultures are equally valid, and they are not (2024).

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Wants school guidance on gender and sex education reviewed; no stated position on whether curricula should include sex education and gender equality.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wants overseas aid cut to fund defence and prisons; supported repurposing the aid budget in 2025.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Praised the British at-sea deterrent but noted parts depend on America; opposed giving it up.

collective-defense.rationale: Called NATO a bedrock of security and wants alliances strengthened through NATO.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said markets need regulation to prevent unfair trading practices, monopolies and exploitation of consumers; voted with the government on the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Bill.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Argues lawfare stops governments delivering what voters chose, and wants to reverse powers moved from Parliament to the courts. She also says she defends the rule of law.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Opposes protectionism and wants diversified supply chains through more trade.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposing differential policing by race is nearby; admissions and hiring not addressed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Said protectionism causes poverty and talent flight, citing Nigeria; advocates more trade not less.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Wants to repeal the Human Rights Act and leave the ECHR, arguing rights come from the common law and Parliament and judges should interpret rather than decide.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Said law should be made by sovereign Parliament accountable to the British people. The monarch's role not addressed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: As minister agreed with the APPG on men and boys, cited male suicide strategy funding and said government should counter stereotypes about boys.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: As equalities minister presented the Sewell report: disparities have many causes besides racism and institutional racism should be applied carefully and based on evidence.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said national interests must come before the ECHR and urged legislating even if lawyers warn it breaches human rights law; promised to leave the ECHR.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Referred to the October 7 attacks as the worst slaughter of Jews since the Holocaust, treating it as established history.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Rejects identity politics as a trap and a source of division, saying no single category such as race or sex should define people.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Blocked Scottish self-ID, wants single-sex spaces by biological sex; but defended the existing certificate route with checks and protection from unfair discrimination.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted against the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill at second reading (Nov 2024) and third reading (June 2025). Vote record only.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Targets radical Islamist ideology and sectarian politics; no statement on Islam as such being incompatible with Western values.

social-market-economy.rationale: Says free markets are not untrammelled and need good regulation, and that the state should provide social security; but also wants a much smaller state and lower taxes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Wants the largest net increase in troops since WWII and 3% of GDP on defence.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Wants Britain to back the US and NATO and show allies what it brings to the table.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Pledges 50,000 more prison places and 10,000 more police officers.

abolish-ip.rationale: Told Cato that intellectual property rights drive innovation and that treating them as protectionism would choke it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Called the UK-US defence base on Diego Garcia crucial and opposed ceding the territory; hosting foreign bases not otherwise addressed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Says she knows what a woman is, welcomed the Supreme Court ruling on biological sex and calls womanhood very biological.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Welcomed the 2025 Supreme Court ruling that woman means biological woman and said she always knew what a woman is.

gm-crops.rationale: Listed the gene-editing rules among Brexit successes that unleash agricultural innovation (2023).

racial-group-interests.rationale: Calls identity politics a trap that sorts people into categories and pits them against each other.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Calls herself a conservative realist and criticised the prime minister for not backing the Iran action promptly, but said nobody sensible would drop bombs without a second thought.

free-public-college.rationale: Said the country cannot keep subsidising young people onto courses that leave debt and poor jobs, and wants thousands of courses cut; as a student criticised protests over £1,000 fees (2024 Times interview).

student-debt-relief.rationale: Wants lower interest on student loans ('end the interest rate ripoff') but also to cut low-value courses; does not propose cancelling debts.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Attacked parties that want Britain to give up its nuclear deterrent, praising crews who delivered continuous at-sea deterrence.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Pledged tougher minimum sentences for the worst crimes (2026).

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Wants immigrants to share British culture and values; no stated position on a language requirement.

voter-id.rationale: As minister defended photographic voter ID in the Elections Bill (2022) and voted for it; proof of citizenship not addressed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said Britain defends a culture where women have the same rights as men.

close-ties-china.rationale: Called China a threat, warned of dangerous dependency, and said Britain must diversify away from it.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: In 2022 suggested better means-testing of winter fuel payments, but in 2024-25 attacked Labour's means-testing of them and backed the Opposition motions to restore them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Criticised crony capitalists who collude with big bureaucracy to rig the system for incumbents and protectionism for special interests (2022).

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Welcomed the Sewell report finding that many factors other than racism drive disparities, while saying racism remains a real force and Britain is not post-racial.

notes: Evidence is mainly her own Commons speeches, speeches and op-eds from 2017 to 2026, and her voting record. Ministerial answers (trade, equalities) are taken as hers when she gave them but are weighed below her later statements as leader. Net zero: in 2024 she defended the 2050 target as set by Parliament; since the 2022 leadership run and 2025-26 she has called for scrapping the legislation. Same-sex marriage and abortion rest on thinner evidence (a ministerial statement, a 2019 abstention, a 2025 post on being pro-choice) and are rated accordingly. Several 2026 conference clips contain other speakers; only her own words were used. Hansard URLs are the debate pages the quoted text was retrieved for through the Hansard search API.
